1.title: Exam Technique and Final Check
1.text: Welcome to Module 18: Exam Technique and Final Check. This is the last module. In part one you will learn how the exam works, how to read a question, what best answers and wrong answers usually look like, and how to plan your last weeks. In part two you will test yourself with fifteen mixed questions.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. State the exam format, and what the open-book rule really allows. Read a question with a method. Recognize what best answers and wrong answers usually do. Plan your pace and your last weeks. And test yourself with fifteen mixed questions.

1.title: The Exam in Numbers
1.text: The exam in numbers. Fifty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes, which is about seventy-two seconds each. You need thirty-seven correct, which is seventy-four percent. The questions are written from the learning objectives and the Scrum Guide. The exam is taken online after the course, it is not proctored, and the timer cannot be paused, though you can bookmark questions. Scrum Alliance offers no practice exam. Always confirm the current format, fees and eligibility on its site before you book.

1.title: Open Book: What It Really Means
1.text: The exam is open book, but be careful what that means. Scrum Alliance's support article says you may use the Scrum Guide and the training materials from your course. A trainer's study guide on the same site allows any written or online resource. Rely on the narrower rule, and confirm the current rule on the site. And think about the clock: at seventy-two seconds a question, you can look up only a handful of items. Know the framework; use the Guide to confirm.

1.title: Reading a Question
1.text: How to read a question. These moves go beyond the Guide, but they work. Read the last sentence first, then the scenario. Think of your own answer before you read the options. Read all four options, perhaps from the bottom up, so that the first reasonable one does not win. Eliminate what you know is wrong. Be careful with absolute words like all, always, never and only, and check them against the Guide. Flag and move on when stuck. Review before you submit.

1.title: Stated, Implied or Absent: A Reminder
1.text: A reminder of a test from Module 15, which practiced it on eleven scenarios. Is the answer stated, implied or absent in the Guide? Stated: the Guide says it, so accept it. Implied: the Guide's logic leads there, so usually accept it. Absent: the Guide never says it, so treat it as not part of Scrum. The Guide is short, so many options turn on exactly this test.

1.title: What the Best Answer Usually Does
1.text: What does the best answer usually do? This is practice, not Guide text. It follows the Guide and keeps Scrum intact. It respects the accountabilities. It asks, coaches or facilitates before telling, but it acts when the team is stuck. It increases transparency, and uses inspection and adaptation. It adapts as soon as possible. It keeps the timeboxes, the Sprint Goal and the quality. It involves the right person. And it serves the whole system: the team, the Product Owner and the organization.

1.title: What the Wrong Answers Usually Do
1.text: And what do wrong answers usually do? This pattern list comes from practice, not from the Guide. They command or manage, for example the Scrum Master assigns tasks. They pick the wrong owner, for example the Scrum Master orders the Product Backlog. They add something Scrum lacks: a project manager, a hardening Sprint, a Sprint zero, or an approval gate. They are passive: wait for the Retrospective. They offer a right action at the wrong time. They use old wording, such as Development Team, the three questions, or servant-leader as a boss. Or they use absolute words.

1.title: Pace and Flagging
1.text: Pace; these exam tips go beyond the Guide. You have about seventy-two seconds a question on average: some questions will take thirty seconds, some will take two minutes. Aim for about a minute on a first pass. That leaves about ten minutes to come back. If a question is stuck, flag it and move on. You can bookmark it, but the clock keeps running. Review before you submit, above all the answers you changed. Do not spend three minutes on one question and lose three others.

1.title: The Three-Week Practice Plan
1.text: A three-week plan; it is the course's suggestion, not part of the Guide. Day one: read the Scrum Guide once in full, then Modules one and two. Week one: Modules three to five, with their questions. Week two: Modules six to twelve, and the Guide's Sprint and artifact sections again. Week three: Modules thirteen to sixteen, which add the workshop and the traps clinic. Redo every question you got wrong. Then take the final check, and a mixed set of fifty questions from the course in sixty minutes. The last two days: Module seventeen, the Guide a second time, and the numbers and technique pages.

1.title: The Last Two Days and Exam Day
1.text: The last two days; these tips go beyond the Guide. Use Module seventeen every day: cover the text and say the facts aloud. Read the Guide a second time; it takes about twenty minutes. On exam day, choose a quiet place and a stable connection, and have the Guide and your course materials ready. Remember that the clock cannot be paused. Start every question with the last sentence. And redo the questions you got wrong earlier; they teach the most.

1.title: What Is Not Exam Content
1.text: A word on scope, so that you do not waste study time. This scope note is exam guidance, not Guide text. The exam draws on the Scrum Guide, the Agile Manifesto, the five Scrum values, and the fifty-two learning objectives. It does not ask for story points, user stories or velocity as required methods. Not Kanban, not scaling frameworks, not fees or renewal rules, and not word-for-word rule drilling for a different exam. Scrum Alliance's own advice names relative story points as something absent from the Guide.

1.title: Part 1 Recap
1.text: Part one recap. Fifty questions, sixty minutes, thirty-seven correct. Open book means the Guide and your course materials, so know the framework. Read the last sentence first, eliminate, and check absolutes. Best answers serve and keep Scrum intact; wrong answers command, add, or wait. Follow the three-week plan, then Module seventeen. The exam tests applying the framework, so practice the method from Module fifteen. Now the final check: fifteen questions, about a minute each.

2.title: Final Check, Question 1
2.text: Question one. At the end of each Sprint the RideLoop team demonstrates progress, but nobody ever changes the Product Backlog or the way the team works afterwards. Which pillar is missing? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, adaptation. Inspection without adaptation is pointless. Transparency is present, and courage is a value, not a pillar.

2.title: Final Check, Question 2
2.text: Question two. In a Retrospective, Sofia wants to raise a conflict with a colleague but fears the reaction. Which two values should the Scrum Master help the team strengthen? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, openness and courage. Raising a hard problem takes the courage to do the right thing, and openness about the work and its challenges.

2.title: Final Check, Question 3
2.text: Question three. What should a Scrum Team do when it has become too large to stay nimble? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. It becomes several cohesive Scrum Teams that share one Product Goal, one Product Backlog and one Product Owner. Team leads, sub-teams and project managers are hierarchies that Scrum does not have.

2.title: Final Check, Question 4
2.text: Question four. A Lakeshore Transit director wants a feature moved to the top of the Product Backlog and approaches Ben directly. What is the best way to handle this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. The director makes the case to Maya, who decides the order. Developers and the Scrum Master do not set the order of the Product Backlog.

2.title: Final Check, Question 5
2.text: Question five. After a successful first Sprint, Lakeshore Transit asks you to help three more teams adopt Scrum. Which response fits the Scrum Master's accountabilities? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The Scrum Master serves the organization by leading, training and coaching its adoption, and advising on rollouts. Managing the teams would create a hierarchy.

2.title: Final Check, Question 6
2.text: Question six. A Lakeshore Transit team works in a fast-changing market with high uncertainty and releases rarely. Which Sprint length best fits the Guide's reasoning? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, a shorter Sprint. It gives more learning cycles and limits risk. Sprints longer than one month are not allowed, and a changing length removes consistency.

2.title: Final Check, Question 7
2.text: Question seven. At Sprint Planning, one top-ordered item is far too large to be finished in a Sprint. What should the Scrum Team do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Refine or split it, so that part of it can be Done within the Sprint, and keep the rest in the Product Backlog.

2.title: Final Check, Question 8
2.text: Question eight. Is the Daily Scrum the only time the Developers can adjust their plan? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. No. The Developers often meet during the day for more detailed discussions about re-planning, and they need no approval to do so.

2.title: Final Check, Question 9
2.text: Question nine. Maya says the Increment may not be given to users until after the Sprint Review. What does the Guide say? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. An Increment may be delivered before the end of the Sprint, and the Review is never a gate to releasing value.

2.title: Final Check, Question 10
2.text: Question ten. How many Product Goals does a Scrum Team work on at a time, and where does the Product Goal live? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. One at a time, in the Product Backlog. The team fulfills or abandons one before taking on the next.

2.title: Final Check, Question 11
2.text: Question eleven. When is the Sprint Goal created? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. During Sprint Planning, and then added to the Sprint Backlog, where it is the commitment. It must be finalized before the event ends.

2.title: Final Check, Question 12
2.text: Question twelve. If the organization has no standard Definition of Done, who creates one? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. The Scrum Team creates one that suits the product, and the Developers conform to it. If a standard exists, it is the minimum.

2.title: Final Check, Question 13
2.text: Question thirteen. The Retrospective produced twenty improvement ideas, and the team wants to pick the few to try next Sprint. Which technique fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, dot voting, which suits selecting several options from a longer list. The Scrum Master facilitates, but does not pick.

2.title: Final Check, Question 14
2.text: Question fourteen. Which description of technical debt is best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. The future cost of rework caused by choosing an easy or limited solution now. It is a metaphor, not money borrowed, and the Guide does not mention it.

2.title: Final Check, Question 15
2.text: Question fifteen. Why can a Sprint horizon that is too long be a problem? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The goal can lose its meaning, and complexity and risk can grow. Shorter Sprints give more learning cycles and limit the cost and effort at risk.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all fifteen answers. One: D. Inspection without adaptation is pointless. Two: A. Openness and courage. Three: C. Several Scrum Teams, one Product Goal and one Product Backlog. Four: B. The director convinces the Product Owner. Five: D. Lead, train and coach the organization. Six: C. Shorter Sprints give more learning and limit risk. Seven: A. Refine or split the large item. Eight: B. The Developers often meet during the day. Nine: A. The Review is never a gate. Ten: D. One Product Goal, in the Product Backlog. Eleven: B. Created in Sprint Planning. Twelve: C. The Scrum Team creates it. Thirteen: B. Dot voting for several options. Fourteen: A. The future cost of rework from shortcuts. Fifteen: D. A long Sprint risks an out-of-date goal. Count how many you got right, and redo the ones you missed, with the module that teaches them. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
